_comment: The single source of truth for what a supervisor agent may start (ADR 0004, docs/design-agent-control.md
'Supervisor scope'). Two implementations read this file: src/lib/config/supervisorPolicy.ts (Vitest) decides
what Settings and the supervisor's launch prompt offer, src-tauri/src/supervisor/policy.rs (cargo test, via
include_str!) decides what actually spawns. If they disagree, the prompt would offer a model the socket
refuses, or the socket would start one nobody was shown. Add a case here before changing either side.
The file is <app_data_dir>/supervisor-policy.json, written by Rust only. Every error fails closed:
nothing the file does not plainly allow is allowed. Paths are canonicalised by Rust before lookup
(realpath); the cases below only cover what is pure: absolute, trailing slash removed.

defaults._comment: What a field that is absent from a valid file means. An absent project entry allows nothing.

reasons._comment: Stable reason keys. Rust sends one as error.reason with code supervisor_denied (checkSpawn) or lists it in parse.rejected (parse). The message beside it is for humans and may change; the key may not.

parse.file_missing: There is no supervisor-policy.json. Nothing is allowed.
parse.malformed: The file is not valid JSON, or not an object. Nothing is allowed.
parse.unsupported_version: The file has a version this build does not know. Nothing is allowed.
parse.invalid_entry: A project entry is not an object, or a field has the wrong type. That project allows nothing.
parse.path_not_absolute: A project key is not an absolute path. That project allows nothing.
parse.bypass_permissions: A project names bypassPermissions as a permission mode. That project allows nothing.

checkSpawn.project_not_listed: The project has no entry in the policy (or the file is missing or unreadable).
checkSpawn.project_not_allowed: The project is listed with allowed: false.
checkSpawn.provider_not_installed: The provider offers no models on this machine.
checkSpawn.provider_not_allowed: The provider is not on this project's supervisor provider list.
checkSpawn.provider_denied_by_project: The project's own provider policy does not permit this provider.
checkSpawn.provider_has_no_models: The policy lists an empty model list for this provider.
checkSpawn.model_not_allowed: The model is not on the policy's model list for this provider.
checkSpawn.model_not_offered: The provider does not offer this model (any more).
checkSpawn.permission_mode_unattended: The permission mode the child would run under (the policy's, or the provider's default when the policy names none) skips permission prompts.
checkSpawn.interactive_not_allowed: An interactive run was requested and the project has allowInteractive: false.
checkSpawn.project_limit_reached: The supervisor already has maxRunning children running in this project.
checkSpawn.global_limit_reached: The supervisor already has maxRunningChildren children running in total.

modelChoice.no_ranked_model: No model was named and none of the allowed models has a size (rank), so none is picked by default.
modelChoice.model_reason_required: The model is large (rank at or above reasonRequiredFromRank) and the spawn names no modelReason.

visibleProjectsRules: Visible = listed with allowed: true. A visible project lists the providers that survive all of:
on the supervisor list (or every offered provider when providers is null), permitted by the project's
provider policy, and left with at least one model. Models are the policy list (or every offered model
when absent) intersected with what the provider offers now, in the provider's own order. Projects are
sorted by path, providers by id. permissionMode is null where the policy names none: the provider's
own default, never the launch defaults.
A provider whose effective permission mode is unattended (permissionModesRules) is left out.

visibleProjects.name: only allowed projects are visible, sorted by path, with the providers and models they offer
providers null lists every offered provider the project policy permits, with all offered models
a listed model the provider no longer offers is not shown
an allowed project whose providers all fall away stays visible with no providers
a provider whose effective mode is unattended is not offered
each visible provider carries its weight, null where the weights do not name it

checkSpawnRules: Checks run in checkOrder; the first that fails is the reason. running counts the calling supervisor's
children with status running: total across projects, byProject per path. Queued counts as running.
A limit is reached when the count is >= the limit. offeredModels is what each installed provider offers
now; a provider missing from it is not installed. projectPolicy is the project's provider policy
(providerPolicy.fixtures.json). On success permissionMode is the policy's value for that provider, or
null; Rust passes it verbatim and the frontend fills in nothing.
permission_mode_unattended: see permissionModesRules; the provider's default counts when the policy names no mode.

project not listed

modelChoiceRules: Which model a supervisor's spawn runs, decided before checkSpawn. offered is what the provider offers (value, rank),
allowed the models the policy leaves for it in that project (visibleProjects' models). request.model null means
the server picks: the allowed model with the smallest rank; unranked models are never picked; a tie goes to the
first in the provider's order. Nothing ranked: no_ranked_model. Then the size gate: if the resolved model is
allowed, offered and its rank is >= reasonRequiredFromRank, a modelReason that is missing or blank is
model_reason_required (the human-facing message names the smaller allowed models). A model outside allowed or
offered passes here untouched: checkSpawn refuses it with its own reason. picked says whether the server chose.

modelChoice.name: no model: the smallest ranked allowed one
no model: the policy's list decides what is smallest
no model: unranked models are never picked
no model and nothing ranked allowed
a named medium model needs no reason
a named large model without a reason
a blank reason is no reason
a named large model with a reason
the largest model with a reason

request.modelReason: The human asked for it by name

modelChoice.name: a named unranked model needs no reason
a picked default that is large still needs a reason
a picked large default with a reason

request.modelReason: Only large models are allowed here

modelChoice.name: a model outside the allowed list is left to checkSpawn

permissionModesRules: Optional on visibleProjects and checkSpawn cases: permissionModes = { provider: { default: string|null, unattended: string[] } }.
unattended lists the modes of that provider that skip permission prompts. Rust derives it from the provider config: a
permissionModes entry marked "unattended": true, bypassPermissions, or a mode whose mapped arguments carry a known skip flag
(--dangerously-*, --yolo, --auto, bypassPermissions). A reviewer mode (Codex --approve-for-me) is attended. The effective mode is the policy's permissionMode for
the provider, else default. A provider missing from permissionModes has default null and no unattended mode.
Unattended effective mode: checkSpawn refuses with permission_mode_unattended; visibleProjects leaves the provider out.
parseMergeRules: Two keys that name one project (after trailing-slash removal here, after realpath in Rust) merge to the stricter
entry: allowed and allowInteractive only if both say so, maxRunning the smaller, providers the intersection (null is everything),
models per provider the intersection where both list it, else the one list. permissionMode: one named mode is kept; two different
modes for one provider make the project allowed: false with permissionMode {} (there is no stricter of two modes).
providerWeights is a load-balancing hint, not a permission: the two entries keep their weights only
when both name the same ones, otherwise the merged project has providerWeights {} (no balancing).
providerWeightsRules: providerWeights: provider id -> an integer 0..99, the share of spawns that provider should get in this project
(load balancing, e.g. {claude: 2, codex: 1}). Advisory only: checkSpawn never reads it. Absent or {} means no
balancing. Keys normalise like provider ids; two keys for one provider keep the smaller weight; a blank key, a
non-integer, a negative number or one above 99 drops the project. visibleProjects reports each provider's
weight, null where the map does not name it.
skillPatternRules: A skill entry is keyed by the absolute path of its folder (the one holding SKILL.md); trailing slashes are dropped.

bash is a list of Claude Code Bash rule patterns, passed as Bash(<pattern>). Blank and repeated patterns are dropped; one containing ( ) " ` \\ or a control character refuses the whole skill entry (invalid_entry), because it would end the rule or split the launch command.
No pattern means the skill loads without a shell. Bash is in the supervisor's tool set only while at least one loaded skill has a pattern.

dirs are folders besides the run folder the file tools may use (passed as --add-dir). Each must be absolute, not the root, and free of the characters a pattern may not hold; otherwise the skill entry is invalid_entry. Trailing slashes are dropped, repeats removed.
Two keys that name one folder keep only the patterns both allow.
Rejected skill entries are listed as { project: null, skill: <key as written>, reason }.
toolRules: A tool entry is keyed by a bare command name (letters, digits and . _ + -, with at least one letter or digit) or by the absolute path of its binary; a path loses its trailing slashes.
Each tool becomes two rules, Bash(<tool>) and Bash(<tool> *): only commands that start with exactly that tool. Claude Code checks each part of a chained command on its own.

A key that is neither a bare name nor an absolute path without whitespace, brackets, quotes, backticks, backslashes, control characters or * (or is /) refuses that entry (invalid_entry); a relative path containing / is path_not_absolute.
dirs work as for skills: extra folders for the file tools (--add-dir), absolute, not the root; otherwise the entry is invalid_entry.
Two keys that name one tool keep only the folders both allow. Bash is in the supervisor's tool set as soon as one tool is approved.
An absolute path whose file is gone at launch is left out, as a missing skill folder is.
Rejected tool entries are listed as { project: null, tool: <key as written>, reason }.
